title: Latency-cost-recall curve exploration: INT8 / GPTQ / AWQ tradeoffs (Jun 2026)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a working exploration of the trade-offs between latency, unit cost, and quality for multiple quantization strategies (INT8/AWQ, GPTQ, FP8 baseline) across different kernel implementations. The goal: produce a small set of recommended inference profiles that map to product SLOs (latency-sensitive vs quality-sensitive) and identify the dominant runtime bottlenecks that limit those profiles.

Background and motivation:
- Prior experiments (see linked PR and JIRA) focused on single-kernel throughput. Here we want a recall-cost curve: for a given degradation in model quality (delta perplexity / human rating), how much latency and $/token do we save?
- We tested on two representative families: 30B and 70B transformer decoders (architecture = standard causal transformer w/ rotary embeddings) using models from the internal catalog (eval snapshots).

High-level methodology:
- Workloads: mix of short-chat (seq_len=64), medium context assistant (seq_len=512), and long context summarization (seq_len=2k).
- Hardware: NVIDIA A100 (40GB) and NVIDIA H100 (80GB) nodes; baseline using default cuBLAS GEMM, compared to two custom kernels: fused-ggml-style matmul (striped 4x packing) and our new fused-kernel (PR 2345) that pre-packs weights into 128B-aligned tiles.
- Quant methods: FP16 baseline, FP8 baseline (where supported), GPTQ (8-bit post-training quant, channel-wise), AWQ (asymmetric weight quant + 4-bit activation-aware mapping), and INT8 trained/aware kernels.
- Quality metrics: validation perplexity on held-out Pile slice, exact-match on a 200-sample HotpotQA subset, and a small human rating panel (N=30) for open-ended instruction prompts (3-step Likert: acceptable/noticeable-buggy/unusable).
- Performance metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per request, tokens/sec throughput at target concurrency, memory resident size (GB), and cost per 1M tokens (derived from our Dedicated pricing baseline).
- Profiling: NVIDIA Nsight sampling, our tracer (token-level timing), and flamegraphs aggregated per-request. We recorded kernel-level breakdowns (matmul, softmax, layernorm, KV memcpy, decode loop overhead).

Key empirical findings (summary):
- Latency & throughput:
  - AWQ-int8 (using our prepack fused-kernel) reduced median token latency by ~1.6x and increased throughput by ~1.8x vs FP16/cuBLAS on A100 for seq_len=64 workloads. Gains persist but diminish for long-context (2k) due to KV-copy costs.
  - GPTQ-8 (channel-wise) improved throughput by ~1.3x on the cuBLAS path but showed worse tail latency; p99 often increased because packing falls back to a slower kernel for odd channel sizes.
  - FP8 (where supported) gave modest gains (~1.2x) but with better quality than AWQ in many cases.
- Quality tradeoffs:
  - On perplexity: AWQ-int8 increased validation perplexity by +6%-9% relative to FP16 (worse on 70B than 30B). GPTQ showed +9%-14% depending on quantization schedule. FP8 stayed within +1%-3%.
  - Human ratings: AWQ produced 78% acceptable, 18% noticeable-buggy, 4% unusable. GPTQ produced 71% acceptable, 24% noticeable-buggy, 5% unusable. FP8: 92% acceptable.
  - HotpotQA exact-match: FP16=0.56, FP8=0.53, AWQ=0.50, GPTQ=0.47. (small sample, trend consistent with perplexity deltas)
- Bottlenecks exposed by profiling:
  - Matmul dominates token-level time for short inputs (~60-72% of token time) -> benefits from pre-packed weights and fused GEMM paths.
  - KV cache copy / reordering is significant and becomes dominant at long contexts (>512 tokens): measured 12%-26% of request time and scales almost linearly with seq_len. Our current memcpy-based path benefits less from quantization speedups.
  - Small kernel overhead (layernorm/softmax) exacerbates p99 for GPTQ due to fallback codepath alignment issues.
  - Dispatcher overhead (per-request routing + token loop in Python worker) is visible at very low token-per-request regimes; adopting our C++ token loop reduces this overhead by ~30% p50.

Representative numeric table (illustrative single-node, A100, 70B model, seq_len=64):
- FP16 (cuBLAS): p50=18ms, p95=45ms, throughput=95 tokens/s, cost=$1.00 per 1M tokens, perplexity=12.1
- FP8 (kernel-a): p50=14.5ms, p95=40ms, throughput=115 tokens/s, cost=$0.86 per 1M tokens, perplexity=12.6
- AWQ-int8 (prepack fused): p50=11.2ms, p95=29ms, throughput=170 tokens/s, cost=$0.58 per 1M tokens, perplexity=13.0
- GPTQ-8 (cuBLAS+packing): p50=13.8ms, p95=55ms, throughput=125 tokens/s, cost=$0.76 per 1M tokens, perplexity=13.6

Observations from the recall-cost curve (quality on x, cost on y):
- AWQ sits in the lower-cost, modest-quality drop quadrant: best candidate for high-throughput, latency-first workloads that can tolerate small quality regressions (e.g., autocomplete, retrieval-augmented fast chat).
- FP8 is a good middle ground when quality matters but some cost improvement is desirable (customer-facing assistants where hallucination risk is non-trivial).
- GPTQ is high variance across models and kernels: sometimes good cost saving for older architectures, but on newer models the kernel fallbacks hurt tail latency, making it less predictable for strict p99 SLOs.

Kernel-specific notes and anomalies:
- Our prepack fused-kernel (PR 2345) shows consistent p50/p95 benefits, but when weight sizes are not aligned to the tile (non multiple of 64 channels) we observe a slow path that doubles matmul time. Action: extend prepack to support ragged tails (owner: Marco).
- cuBLAS path with GPTQ often incurs extra transposes and small-buffer GEMMs that are not efficiently batched; this explains the p99 regressions. Suggest adding a small-batch GEMM aggregator to reduce kernel launch overhead for small micro-batches.
- KV cache write pattern: copying from GPU-local decoding buffers to persistent KV layout triggers a lot of device-to-device overhead. Fusion idea: write decode output already in KV layout to avoid an extra pass.

Cost accounting quick note:
- Cost numbers use our Dedicated per-hour pricing and assume ~70% GPU utilization; actual cloud egress and infra overhead not included. Use them as relative comparisons, not absolute pricing.

Immediate recommendations (actionable):
1) Ship an "AWQ-latency" inference profile: prepack fused-kernel + AWQ-int8 weights + short-context optimized KV path. Target: p50 < 12ms for seq_len=64 on 70B. (Owner: Priya; ETA: 2 sprints)
2) Stabilize prepack kernel tails: add ragged-channel support and unit tests for odd channel sizes. (Owner: Marco Nguyen; ETA: 3 weeks)
3) Add micro-batch GEMM aggregator for GPTQ fallback paths to reduce kernel launch overhead and p99. (Owner: Ethan Morales; linked PR idea)
4) Long-context optimization spike: prototype writing decode output directly into KV layout and measure KV-copy elimination; expected p99 improvements for seq_len >512. (Owner: Sofia Iqbal; ETA: exploratory 2 weeks)
5) Conservative product guidance: default hosted API "fast" tier can use AWQ-int8 profile; "balanced" keep FP8; "high-quality" keep FP16 or FP8 with QA gating. Document risks and per-model flags. (Product + Docs)

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- How AWQ quality scales with calibration dataset size and whether a small 1k-sample calibration reduces human-facing failure modes.
- Can mixed-precision kernels (FP8 activations + INT8 weights) get the best of both worlds? We have partial support; need a controlled sweep.
- Impact of different attention rematerialization strategies on memory/perf tradeoffs with int8 kernels.
- Evaluate on H100 microarchitecture: preliminary runs show similar relative gains but different absolute p99 shape. Need full sweep for production recommendation.

Appendix: short troubleshooting log (notes from profiling runs)
- Jun 16: observed a flaky p99 spike when running GPTQ inference with concurrency=8; root cause was a mutex in our allocator used only by the fallback kernel. Fixed in local branch.
- Jun 18: AWQ prepack produced ~1% quality variance between runs — traced to nondeterministic rounding in prepack pass on H100. Need deterministic build flag.

References and links:
- PR with fused prepack kernel: github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2345
- JIRA ticket for rollout gating: INF-9876
- Playbook (living doc): confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Quantization-Playbook

Next steps: agree on which profiles to expose in console (fast / balanced / quality), prioritize kernel fixes (ragged tail & small-batch GEMM aggregator), and schedule a 1-week long H100 sweep across the same matrix.

If you want raw data: I uploaded aggregated CSVs to the experiments bucket (see Slack thread). I'll push a cleaned CSV and the flamegraphs to the confluence page once this doc is stable.

-- Priya
